dedupe_keys.name: soweto south africa cost benefit analysis of a municipal solid waste recycling facility

description: This case study appraises whether a facility recycling municipal solid waste into raw materials for industry would pay off in Soweto, the large township of Johannesburg, South Africa. Olusola Olaitan Ayeleru, Felix Okonta and Freeman Ntuli of the University of Johannesburg, with the Botswana International University of Science and Technology, based the analysis on historic data from the municipality and recent waste composition data, and published it in Waste Management in 2021. The cost-benefit calculation was done in Excel and checked in MATLAB, Python and R, with a sensitivity analysis. It gave an internal rate of return of 42 percent on investment and 98 percent on equity, a net present value of about 63 million rand (about 4.6 million US dollars), a break-even throughput of 211 tonnes of waste, total recycling benefits of about 486 million rand and about 677 potential jobs. The article is available online by subscription, and the abstract is free on PubMed. Coverage is one proposed facility. Caveats: the underlying municipal and composition data are not published, and the valuation of benefits depends on assumed material prices. Simulation uses: costs, throughput and returns for recycling facilities in investment appraisal of urban waste systems. Related records: the China domestic waste system dynamics cost-benefit study (case_study-china-domestic-waste-management-system-dynamics-cost-benefit-2100) appraises waste options at national scale.
